title: Cell Biology & Photosynthesis Quiz
description: Comprehensive assessment covering cellular structure, chloroplast functions, and light-dependent reactions.

questions.question: What is the primary function of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll pigments absorb solar radiation, primarily blue and red wavelengths, driving photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which organelle is universally referred to as the powerhouse of the eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions through ATP production.

questions.question: What is the main byproduct gas released during oxygenic photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Water molecules are split during light reactions, releasing oxygen gas as a byproduct.

questions.question: Which cellular structure regulates what enters and exits the cell?
questions.explanation: The semi-permeable phospholipid bilayer selectively regulates transport of molecules.

title: Algebra & Linear Equations Speed Quiz
description: Weekly speed quiz on solving multi-step linear equations, variables isolation, and algebraic expressions.

questions.question: Solve for x: 3x + 12 = 33
questions.explanation: Subtract 12 from both sides to get 3x = 21, then divide by 3 to get x = 7.

questions.question: What is the slope (m) of the linear equation y = -4x + 9?
questions.explanation: In slope-intercept form y = mx + c, the coefficient of x is the slope, which is -4.

questions.question: If 2x - 4 = x + 6, find the value of x.
questions.explanation: Subtract x from both sides: x - 4 = 6. Add 4: x = 10.

title: Computer Networks & Internet Protocols
description: Assessment on IP addressing, OSI 7-layer model, DNS, and fundamental cybersecurity protocols.

questions.question: Which protocol is responsible for translating domain names into IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable hostnames into machine-readable IP addresses.

questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses formatted as 4 octets.

questions.question: Which port number is conventionally used for secure HTTPS web traffic?
questions.explanation: Port 443 is designated for Transport Layer Security (HTTPS).

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model handles end-to-end packet routing across networks?
questions.explanation: Layer 3 (Network Layer) is responsible for logical routing and packet forwarding.

title: Chemical Bonding & Valency Assessment
description: Completed diagnostic test on ionic vs covalent bonds, electron sharing, and periodic table families.

questions.question: What type of bond is formed when electrons are completely transferred between atoms?
questions.explanation: Ionic bonds occur through the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer.

questions.question: What is the valency of Carbon in methane (CH4)?
questions.explanation: Carbon has 4 valence electrons and forms 4 covalent bonds, making it tetravalent.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is formed predominantly by covalent bonding?
questions.explanation: Water is formed by shared electron pairs between hydrogen and oxygen atoms.

questions.question: Noble gases are chemically inert primarily because they have:
questions.explanation: Full octet or duplet in their outer shell provides maximum stability.
